To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) orthologous RdRP enzymes can undergo rapid amino acid sequence divergence; (2) the enzymatic activities of orthologous enzymes can diverge significantly; (3) the overall protein fold and oligomeric state are conserved; and (4) the enzymatic activity of the enzyme can diverge without a significant change of the overall protein fold.

the orthologous RNA-dependent RNA polymerases QDE-1 from the fungi Neurospora crass, Thielavia terreris, and Myceliopthorh thermophila show considerable differences in their enzymatic activity in vitro, despite having similar protein structures.

(i) QDE-1 from Neurospora crass, a key enzyme of the quelling RNAi pathway, is a homodimer in solution and in complex with a template, and (ii) the homologs of Qde-1 from two related fungi, Thelavia terrestris and Myceliopthora thermophila, have diverged in enzymatic activities but retained the overall protein fold and the quaternary structure of QDE-Ncr.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution and molecular mechanisms of RNA silencing in eukaryotes.
the evolution of RdRP enzymes and the mechanisms of their action.
the evolution of RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRP), which play a crucial role in RNA silencing pathways in eukaryotes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RdRPs can undergo functional divergence during evolution, which can lead to a change in the mode of action.
the RdRP family of enzymes is a very dynamic group that has undergone rapid divergence in evolution.
the RdRP family is highly diverse and flexible in terms of structure and activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QDE-1 orthologs from N. crssa, T. terrestris, and M. thermophila can all catalyze RNA synthesis, but their precise modes of action are different.
functional divergence of orthologs can occur in RdRPs, and the functional divergence is not necessarily accompanied with structural divergence.
functional evolution in RdRPs can occur in the absence of structural changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
functional changes in orthologs can be achieved through subtle alterations in the protein sequence that are not necessarily associated with major changes in protein fold.
the evolution of RNA silencing pathways is likely to be driven by changes in enzymatic activities of RdRPs rather than by the emergence of novel enzymes.

the evolution of RdRPs can proceed in two different ways: (i) via the duplication of a single gene that can give rise to paralogous enzymes with distinct enzymatic activities and (ii) via the divergence of orthologs that can lead to functional specialization of individual members of a paralogous group.
